A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DYDECOMP research work. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original verification experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, and sensitivity analyses on FActScore-derived ChatGPT and PerplexityAI claims, including Tables 1, 2, and 5.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experimental results and adds qualitative decomposition outputs in Appendix E, Table 6.

M1.justification: The iterative binary decomposition procedure, breadth-first scheduling, GRU atomicity state, confidence-change reward, and PPO training remain unchanged in Section 2 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same FActScore-derived ChatGPT and PerplexityAI biography claims across atomicities -1 through 4. The added appendix examples remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 5 retain FActScore, FActScore-Atom, WICE, and R-ND. New Table 6 illustrates three existing baselines without changing comparator membership in the retained experiments.

E3.justification: The data splits, sample counts, atomicity ranges, models, verification policies, metrics, and training budgets are unchanged. Table 6 uses an already evaluated DeepSeek-V3/Llama3-Inst-8B No-Context configuration.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a qualitative comparison of decomposition outputs, while Appendix B.2 supplies paired data examples for the new case-study discussion. Existing ablations, training-data sensitivity tests, and information-loss analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed, uncertainty, and significance-reporting practices are unchanged. Figure 2 retains the same Pearson correlation analysis, and the new examples introduce no statistical estimation.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results in Tables 1, 2, and 5 and Figures 2, 4–6 are unchanged. Table 6 adds Sabatini decomposition outputs: DYDECOMP produces 2 subclaims, versus 8 for FActScore, 11 for R-ND, and 7 for WICE.

T1.justification: The atomicity definition, bilevel optimization and MDP formulations, reward equations, and PPO/advantage derivations are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the atomicity-misalignment claim, the 4.73M-parameter reinforcement-learning contribution, and the headline 0.07 confidence and 0.12 accuracy improvement claims.

C2.justification: New Section 4.3 substantially qualifies the confidence-as-accuracy-proxy interpretation by acknowledging confidence over-optimization without corresponding accuracy gains. It attributes dataset differences to claim complexity and verifier capability, making capability a central applicability condition. Appendix E adds an atomicity-matching interpretation of the new example.

D1.justification: Initialization, BERT/UNLI usage, prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, training time, and code/model access information are retained. Training initialization and hyperparameters move from Appendices B.2/B.3 to B.3/B.4 without substantive changes.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged. Appendix A newly calls dynamic decomposition the first solution to the stated static-policy limitations, while Section 5.1 reframes its role from addressing over-decomposition to addressing over-optimization through controllability.

P1.justification: V2 adds Section 4.3 and Appendices B.2/E, renumbers affected subsections, revises a few explanatory passages, and corrects Llama3-Int-8B to Llama3-Inst-8B. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds two boxed data examples and Table 6, extends Figure 1's caption, adjusts table spacing, and reflows existing displays. Existing figures retain their graphical content; the front page also gains an ACL'25 header.

improvement.justification: V2 usefully acknowledges confidence–accuracy failures and supplies concrete examples. However, new Section 4.3 describes negligible ChatGPT accuracy improvements despite retained Table 1 showing substantial baseline-relative losses, such as DYDECOMP's 0.509 versus FActScore's 0.809 at atomicity 2 with No-Context verification. Appendix E also claims an optimum of 2 where Figure 4 peaks at 0. These inconsistencies undermine the added explanations, leaving the net balance of improved transparency and misleading interpretation uncertain.
